newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies to start Cardoso re-election push.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies to start Cardoso re-election push.

text.p: A proposal that President Fernando Henrique Cardoso be given the chance of a second term was due to begin its passage through Congress on Tuesday, a congressional official said.
A special committee in the Chamber of Deputies was scheduled to take place at 1430 local/1630 GMT, the official said.
The committee has up to 40 sessions, each equivalent to a working day, to vote on the proposed constitutional amendment which, if approved, would advance to the floor of the lower house.
The amendment would allow presidents, state governors and mayors to stand for a second term. Brazil's constitution limits holders of executive office to one term.
The committee will have 30 seats, although three left-wing opposition parties have said they will not put forward any members because they oppose the idea of re-election.

Observers say the government should have little trouble getting the amendment through the committee and that the real battle will be on the floor of the turbulent lower house where it needs two three-fifths majorities.

News reports said two big government allies in Congress, the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) and the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), would name their members of the committee shortly before its first meeting.
The PMDB had been split over re-election between its old guard leadership, which wanted to put off dealing with the issue until 1997, and its pro-reform wing.
PPB president Sen. Esperidiao Amin was quoted as saying the party would today name its members and that a party convention on December 4 would determine how they should vote.
The PPB leadership includes outgoing Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf whose own presidential ambitions might turn the party against Cardoso's re-election plans.
